mcqs.question: Three systems A, B and C are such that A is in thermal equilibrium with C, and B is also in thermal equilibrium with C. Which of the following comparisons correctly reflects the implication of the Zeroth law?

options.A: System A may have a different temperature from system B.
options.B: System A and system B must be in thermal equilibrium with each other.
options.C: Only system C is guaranteed to have a uniform temperature throughout.
options.D: Thermal equilibrium is not transitive; no conclusion can be drawn about A and B.

mcqs.answer: System A and system B must be in thermal equilibrium with each other.
mcqs.explanation: The Zeroth law states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other. Hence A and B must have the same temperature and be in equilibrium. Options A, C and D contradict this transitive property.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement
mcqs.question: A mercury thermometer is calibrated using ice‑water (0 °C) and boiling water (100 °C at 1 atm). According to the Zeroth law, why can this same thermometer be used to determine the temperature of any other system?

options.A: Because the thermometer reaches thermal equilibrium with each reference system, establishing fixed temperature points.
options.B: Because mercury expands linearly with temperature, providing a direct scale.
options.C: Because heat always flows from a hotter to a colder body.
options.D: Because temperature is defined as the average kinetic energy of molecules.

mcqs.answer: Because the thermometer reaches thermal equilibrium with each reference system, establishing fixed temperature points.
mcqs.explanation: The Zeroth law guarantees that when the thermometer is in thermal equilibrium with the ice‑water and boiling‑water baths, it records the same temperature as those systems. Once calibrated, any other system placed in contact with the thermometer will also reach equilibrium, allowing the thermometer to read its temperature. Options B, C and D describe unrelated facts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly states the Zeroth law of thermodynamics?

options.A: If two systems are in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
options.B: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.
options.C: The entropy of an isolated system always increases.
options.D: Heat flows spontaneously from a colder body to a hotter body.

mcqs.answer: If two systems are in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
mcqs.explanation: Option A is the exact wording of the Zeroth law, establishing temperature as a transitive property. Option B is the First law, C is the Second law, and D is the opposite of the natural direction of heat flow.

mcqs.question: Two bodies are said to be in thermal equilibrium when:

options.A: They are at the same temperature and no net heat flows between them.
options.B: They have the same mass and specific heat capacity.
options.C: They are made of the same material.
options.D: They are isolated from the surroundings.

mcqs.answer: They are at the same temperature and no net heat flows between them.
mcqs.explanation: Thermal equilibrium is defined by equal temperatures and the absence of net heat transfer. The other options describe unrelated conditions.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes temperature from heat in the context of the Zeroth law?

options.A: Temperature is a scalar property that determines the direction of heat flow; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
options.B: Temperature is the total kinetic energy of a system; heat is the temperature measured by a thermometer.
options.C: Temperature and heat are interchangeable terms describing the same physical quantity.
options.D: Heat is a property of a system at equilibrium, while temperature only exists during heat transfer.

mcqs.answer: Temperature is a scalar property that determines the direction of heat flow; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
mcqs.explanation: The Zeroth law uses temperature as the quantity that becomes equal when systems are in thermal equilibrium. Heat, on the other hand, is the energy transferred due to a temperature difference. Options B, C and D misrepresent the definitions.

mcqs.question: Metal block X is placed in contact with metal block Y, and both reach a steady temperature. Block Y is then placed in contact with metal block Z, and after some time Z also reaches the same steady temperature as Y. What can be concluded about blocks X and Z?

options.A: Blocks X and Z are at the same temperature and are in thermal equilibrium.
options.B: Blocks X and Z may have different temperatures because they never touched each other.
options.C: Only block Y is guaranteed to be at the same temperature as X and Z.
options.D: The situation violates the Zeroth law.

mcqs.answer: Blocks X and Z are at the same temperature and are in thermal equilibrium.
mcqs.explanation: By the Zeroth law, if X is in equilibrium with Y and Y is in equilibrium with Z, then X and Z must also be in equilibrium, meaning they share the same temperature. Options B, C and D ignore the transitive nature of thermal equilibrium.

mcqs.question: Two identical cups of water are initially at different temperatures. After placing them in contact for a long time, they reach the same temperature. Which statement best describes this observation?

options.A: The cups have achieved thermal equilibrium, so no net heat flows between them.
options.B: Heat has been created in the system, raising the temperature of both cups.
options.C: The cups will continue to exchange heat indefinitely.
options.D: One cup must have lost mass to equalize the temperatures.

mcqs.answer: The cups have achieved thermal equilibrium, so no net heat flows between them.
mcqs.explanation: When two bodies reach the same temperature, they are in thermal equilibrium and the net heat flow stops. Options B, C and D are incorrect because heat is conserved, flow stops at equilibrium, and mass is unchanged.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement
mcqs.question: A student places a calibrated thermometer in a beaker of water. After the mercury column stops moving, the reading is 45 °C. The same thermometer is then placed in another beaker of unknown liquid, and the mercury column again stops moving. What does the Zeroth law guarantee about the temperature reading of the second liquid?

options.A: If the mercury column stops at the same height, the second liquid is also at 45 °C.
options.B: The second liquid must be hotter than 45 °C because it was unknown.
options.C: The thermometer cannot be used for the second liquid because it was calibrated only for water.
options.D: The reading will be lower than 45 °C because liquids cool the thermometer.

mcqs.answer: If the mercury column stops at the same height, the second liquid is also at 45 °C.
mcqs.explanation: When the thermometer reaches thermal equilibrium with any system, it reads the temperature of that system. By the Zeroth law, identical equilibrium readings imply identical temperatures, regardless of the substance. Options B, C and D misunderstand the principle of temperature measurement.
